const r=load("detector_root");
const content=`# Four-detector evaluation of recovered baseline — November 10, 2026

**All four supplied models completed inference and returned CLEAN: zero of four Trojan votes. Exact full-design graph extraction failed. The successful scores are classifications of the package's heuristic fallback graph, not proof that the complete baseline is Trojan-free.**

The candidate was the unchanged recovered baseline, not the readiness-repaired derivative, AES teaching reference, or regenerated-bitstream decode. Its SHA-256 is 180b895d9e3ada5f662ee502277db1eedcfd80bd53fbf29d9a612fcc3e1b1765.

## Actual results

| Model | Predicted class | P(clean), model score | P(Trojan), model score |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| HT1 | CLEAN | 0.92415720 | 0.07584280 |
| HT2 | CLEAN | 0.64483154 | 0.35516843 |
| HT3 | CLEAN | 0.78389078 | 0.21610928 |
| HT4 | CLEAN | 0.95355976 | 0.04644027 |

The supplied ensemble rule labels a design TROJAN if any model predicts class 1; otherwise it labels it CLEAN. Here the result is **CLEAN, 0/4 votes**. Mean P(Trojan) is 0.17339019, maximum 0.35516843 and minimum 0.04644027. These are classifier outputs and descriptive aggregates, not calibrated probabilities of real hardware compromise.

The completed process returned **exit 0**, with empty stderr and no timeout. Four different checkpoint files and their serialized tensor payloads were independently verified as distinct. Every checkpoint loaded strictly with no missing/unexpected tensor keys, on CPU in evaluation mode.

[Full results](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection_02/RESULTS.json), [raw stdout](@ROOT@/records/detector_02.stdout), [exact command/result](@ROOT@/records/detector_02_command.json), [checkpoint identities](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection_02/model_loads.json).

## Extraction failure and coverage limits

The actual exact-extraction failure was:

> No such module: SBRAM404K

The input contains four SB_RAM40_4K instances but no definitions or include directives for their behavioral implementations. The package's preprocessing removes underscores globally, hence the name SBRAM404K in the exception. It then takes its own built-in heuristic fallback. This was not a fallback invented to obtain a favorable prediction.

Observed fallback graph:
- 5,728 nodes and 10,947 directed edges.
- One weakly connected component.
- 2,848 raw signal nodes and **2,880 operation nodes, all labeled generic branch**.
- After supplied normalization: 2,771 signal, 2,880 branch, 38 input and 39 output feature labels. These are graph-feature labels assigned by the package, not a physical port inventory.
- Four of the available 37 feature categories occur.
- No empty/dummy graph was accepted.

These limitations materially weaken the interpretation:
1. **RAM-body semantics are absent.** This is not complete elaboration of the working simulation model; its external primitive library was not supplied to this detector run.
2. **The graph is coarse.** Assignment dependencies and generic branch labels do not fully represent LUT behavior, timing, sequential/control conditions, hierarchy or memory behavior.
3. **Text preprocessing is representation-sensitive.** The package removes comments/underscores and renames the top in a disposable preprocessing file. The resulting graph is not independently proved semantically equivalent to the original.
4. **Applicability is unvalidated.** These pretrained classifiers' accuracy, calibration and training-distribution fit on this recovered FPGA netlist have not been established. A single baseline run cannot measure sensitivity, false-negative rates or general reliability.
5. **Functional equivalence and security classification are separate.** This result does not replace the prior functional proofs, fix the baseline readiness limitation, prove algorithm correctness or establish physical-board security.

The appropriate claim is: **“HT1–HT4 did not flag the heuristic graph extracted from the unchanged recovered baseline.”** Do not claim that four independent complete-design security analyses certified the hardware.

[Extraction output](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection_02/extraction.stdout), [preprocessing audit](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection_02/preprocessing.json), [graph before normalization](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection_02/graph_before_normalization.json), [exact model inputs](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection_02/model_input.json).

## Method and reproducibility

A fresh isolated folder contains byte-identical copies of the recovered source and supplied course package. The recovered file is 1,213,314 bytes / 45,711 lines with top module chip. The functional-role adapter was copied for provenance but not fed to the detector, avoiding a wrapper-only graph.

The detector-only runner uses the supplied HW2GRAPH, DataProcessor and graph neural-network classes without modifying those package files. It follows the same exact-first and automatic heuristic-fallback path used by the notebook. No large lookup-table shortcut was triggered. A 30-second extraction bound was configured; the actual missing-module failure/fallback completed in under one second and did not time out.

All four configurations use 37→200→200 graph convolutions, SAGPooling ratio 0.8, max readout and a 200→2 output layer. The runner preserves the supplied 37-feature vocabulary and normalization, uses the same log-softmax/argmax calculation and any-positive-vote ensemble rule, and requires all four models rather than accepting a partial ensemble. CPU inference uses seed 0, one thread and evaluation mode.

Two disclosed inference-only adaptations:
- Checkpoints are read with weights_only=True and strict state loading. No checkpoint changes or model training occurred.
- The training graph pickle is not loaded. Source review confirmed that it only adds cached graphs and initializes the fixed feature count; the notebook selects the last appended candidate graph for inference. The same static 37-feature mapping is preserved. Cached labels or statistics do not enter the forward calculation.

The graph's label=0 field is the notebook's placeholder metadata. It is not a verified ground-truth label and is not passed into the model's x/edge_index/batch forward calculation.

Environment: native macOS 26.2 arm64, Python 3.12.1, PyTorch 2.10.0, PyTorch Geometric 2.3.1, PyVerilog 1.3.0, NetworkX 3.2.1 and PyGraphviz 2.0.4. Full dependencies, locations and installation logs are retained. The environment uses a local venv with shared site packages; it is not a completely self-contained deployment. The package recommends Python 3.10/3.11; this execution instead verified the required imports and inference on the available 3.12.1 interpreter. Compatibility beyond this run is not claimed.

[Runner](@ROOT@/run_detectors.py), [environment summary](@ROOT@/records/environment_summary.json), [dependency/setup commands](@ROOT@/records/environment_commands.jsonl), [independent review](@ROOT@/records/input_audit/INDEPENDENT_RUN_REVIEW.md).

## Failures preserved

- Runtime setup initially lacked PyGraphviz. A native wheel installed inside the isolated venv supplied the required Graphviz libraries; import/layout checks passed.
- Shared PyArrow/Safetensors binaries had the wrong CPU architecture. Same-version native wheels were installed only inside the venv. Other dependency compatibility changes are recorded.
- The first detector launch returned exit 1 before loading models because PYTHONNOUSERSITE exposed an incompatible global x86_64 PyTorch installation. Its traceback and command are retained. The second launch used the verified native shared user-site PyTorch; candidate, package and runner were unchanged.
- Exact graph extraction failed on the missing RAM module. The original package catches that exception, prints its message, cleans some parser scratch files and falls back. The available error message is retained; no nonexistent full backend traceback is claimed.

The first launch produced no detector result. Only baseline_detection_02 provides the four scores above.

[First failed launch](@ROOT@/records/detector.stderr), [first command/result](@ROOT@/records/detector_command.json), [failed run record](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection/failure.txt).

## Independent review, preservation and logs

A separate reviewer checked 25 conditions, including source/package identity, distinct checkpoint payloads, graph transformation/normalization, exact model-input ordering, strict loading, inference equations and ensemble calculations. It found the stored numbers consistent within float precision and no hidden fallback. This was a read-only evidence review, not an independent retraining or security assessment.

All **138 source/copy/original hash checks** passed. The project repository remains clean at a3006f61f55fd8b6a232377d292fcec3138bf1ae. Recovered RTL, original challenge files, source course package and user repository were unchanged.

No solution material, generation/repair/evasion loop, AI gateway, key extraction, training or board programming was used. Network access was limited to installing ordinary runtime dependencies; source RTL was not sent to an AI service.

[Preservation receipt](@ROOT@/records/preservation_check.json), [AI-record index and gaps](@ROOT@/AI_RECORD.md). Native visible-record snapshots and raw experiment logs are preserved separately. The output manifest records the evidence files and its explicit scope; installation caches/runtime dependencies are documented rather than mistaken for experimental results.
`.replaceAll("@ROOT@",r);
text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: "+r+"/REPORT.md\n"+content.split("\n").map(x=>"+"+x).join("\n")+"\n*** End Patch"));

content.text:
The independent review confirmed that four distinct checkpoints were used, the baseline was unchanged, and the reported scores match the saved model inputs and outputs.

It also found that all 2,880 operation nodes in the fallback graph became generic “branch” nodes. That is another reason to treat these as limited detector results. I’m sealing the report, failure logs, and AI-record export now.

const r=load("detector_root");
const ai=`# AI records — defensive baseline detector run

This is an authored index, not a reconstructed verbatim conversation.

The user request was: “Run the four TrojanGYM detectors on our recovered baseline in a separate copy and report the results and limitations. Preserve AI logs, keep my repo unchanged, and don’t use solutions.”

## Authentic records retained

[EXPORT_INDEX.json](@ROOT@/records/current_task_transcripts/EXPORT_INDEX.json) indexes a bounded visible-record snapshot of the root task and two child sessions: runtime preparation and independent input/result review. It contains **200 records**, with **1,410 retained fields** and source-line hashes verified, plus a 26-file checksum inventory.

The exact task begins at native root line 1102, 2026-11-10T12:20:14.739Z. The snapshot completed at 12:27:30.124586Z; the last root event retained is 12:27:25.766Z. Each session has its own read window.

Available records include the user's request, visible assistant messages, tool invocations/results, command-execution outputs and file-change records. Original fields were preserved and checked, not paraphrased into a fake transcript.

## Explicit gaps

- Collaboration prompt/message bodies encrypted in the native source remain unavailable as readable text; no decryption or reconstruction was attempted.
- The current final reply, later report/AI-index writing and final sealing actions are outside the snapshot. Saved files and experiment receipts document those actions, not an invented native transcript.
- Earlier mixed coordinator history, unrelated conversations, reasoning, instructions and compaction payloads were excluded.
- Some tool outputs may already be truncated; standalone runtime/detector logs preserve full outputs where captured.
- The export is local and filtered. Hash/field consistency checks do not prove complete conversation coverage, authenticate serving-model weights or establish third-party provenance.
- The export-only agent's final response is outside the three-session snapshot. No public chat-share link was created.

## Actual actions and evidence

A fresh directory received unchanged copies of the baseline, adapter and supplied course package. The runtime agent prepared a venv-local inference environment, retaining installation/import failures and fixes. The review agent checked input suitability, fixed feature mapping, cache omission and later the completed detector result. No agent was assigned generation, evasion, training or key work.

The parent wrote a detector-only runner using unchanged package classes. It required all four distinct checkpoints, strict weights-only loading, CPU evaluation and a nonempty graph. Source hashes and the original inference/ensemble calculation were preserved. The dataset pickle was not deserialized; its omission was reviewed and disclosed.

The first launch failed before inference because a user-site override exposed incompatible global PyTorch. Its exact error remains. The second launch corrected only that environment selection. Exact graph extraction then failed on the missing RAM module; the package's automatic heuristic fallback produced the graph used for all four classifiers. No input was altered or optimized in response to the model scores.

[First failure](@ROOT@/records/detector.stderr), [successful execution log](@ROOT@/records/detector_02.stdout), [successful command/exit receipt](@ROOT@/records/detector_02_command.json), [results](@ROOT@/runs/baseline_detection_02/RESULTS.json), [environment setup records](@ROOT@/records/environment_commands.jsonl).

The independent reviewer verified 25 conditions and highlighted the missing RAM semantics and generic branch-only operation features. The final report states these limitations alongside the four CLEAN graph classifications, with no claim of complete-design security.

Original source, package and original-challenge checks all passed; repository status/HEAD were unchanged. No solutions, repository edits, board actions, AI gateway calls, generated Trojans or detector-guided evasion occurred.

[Technical report](@ROOT@/REPORT.md), [preservation check](@ROOT@/records/preservation_check.json), [independent review](@ROOT@/records/input_audit/INDEPENDENT_RUN_REVIEW.md). Runtime installation contents and other evidence are inventoried separately; the existing AI records and earlier experiments remain intact.
`.replaceAll("@ROOT@",r);
